figure: Figure 17.1 (Sizing a fleet of one model)
issue: Two annotations with different referents are set on one in-plot text line, producing a false clause: 'N-1 residual (~6.0 ideal, ρ = 1) headroom 2.5 req/s (8.0 − 5.5)' reads as 'the N-1 residual has 2.5 req/s of headroom'. The N-1 headroom over the ~5.5 req/s burst is 6.0 − 5.5 = 0.5 req/s; 2.5 req/s is the full 4-host fleet's headroom (8.0 − 5.5). In grayscale the color coding that might separate the two referents is lost, and a reader who screenshots or quotes the figure gets a failover margin inflated 5x.
evidence: Verbatim figure text (PDF 302): 'N-1 residual (~6.0 ideal, ρ = 1) headroom 2.5 req/s (8.0 − 5.5)'. Recompute: N-1 residual = 3 hosts x 2.0 = 6.0 req/s; margin vs burst = 6.0 - 5.5 = 0.5 req/s. N=4 headroom = 8.0 - 5.5 = 2.5 req/s. Caption on the same page states the correct value: 'at ideal ρ = 1 the N−1 = 3 residual (~6.0 req/s) clears the ~5.5 burst with ~0.5 req/s margin'. The figure's own top-right note also treats N-1 as tight (ρ ≥ 0.917), contradicting a 2.5 req/s N-1 headroom.
acceptance_test: The rendered figure contains no line on which 'N-1 residual' and '2.5 req/s' are contiguous; the two annotations are split (separate lines/positions), and any headroom figure adjacent to the N-1 label equals 0.5 req/s (6.0 − 5.5) or is explicitly attributed to the N=4 line as 'N=4 headroom 2.5 = 8.0 − 5.5'.

issue: The green annotation box 'cloud $87.6K/mo (occupancy input) / priced at 6.24M req/mo only' is drawn opaquely over the plot area and occludes the managed-API dashed line and the shaded price band over roughly x ≈ 1e6–3e6 requests/month; both series disappear behind the box and re-emerge on either side.
evidence: Rendered page (PDF 298): the red band and red dashed managed line are visible in the lower-left and again above/right of the green box, with the box's white background covering the segment between. Geometry confirms the collision: managed line y = 0.0208x and band y = 0.015x–0.025x both pass through the box's vertical range (≈2.5e4–1.2e5 USD/mo) at x ≈ 1.2e6–5.8e6, overlapping the box's horizontal span; the band at x = 2e6 (y = 3e4–5e4) lies inside the box.
acceptance_test: At 100% zoom the managed-API dashed line and the price band are continuous across the full x-axis with no segment hidden behind the annotation box (box relocated to a clear region with a leader line, or given an edge-only/transparent background so the underlying curves show through).

issue: The caption states the figure 'marks the canonical-price point (star) and the full sensitivity span (horizontal line)', but by construction every break-even point for the $15–25/1K band lies on the self-host line (y = $155,816.93/mo), so the sensitivity-span horizontal line is drawn exactly on top of the blue self-host line, and the 6.2–10.4M interval covers only log10(10.4/6.2) ≈ 0.23 of the 4-decade x-axis (~6% of axis width). At 150 dpi no end caps or ticks are visible, so the span cannot be told apart from the line it annotates and the 'region, not a point' message rests on the red text box alone.
evidence: Caption (PDF 298): 'The figure marks the canonical-price point (star) and the full sensitivity span (horizontal line)'. Recompute: break-even satisfies 155,816.93 = price_per_request x V, so all break-even y-values equal the self-host cost by construction; span width = log10(10.4/6.2)/4 ≈ 0.057 of the x-axis. Rendered-page inspection at 150 dpi: no distinguishable end markers on the self-host line between 6.2e6 and 1.04e7.
acceptance_test: The 6.2M and 10.4M endpoints are individually visible at print size (end caps/ticks on the span, or an x-axis bracket labeled '6.2M' and '10.4M'), and the star at ≈7.5M is visually separable from the self-host line; alternatively the caption drops the '(horizontal line)' claim if the span is not drawn with endpoints.

issue: The caption renders the caching formula with unbalanced parentheses — 'the in-plot note's f(r)=S+P/r)/(S+P)' has a closing paren after 'P/r' with no matching opener — while the in-plot note itself correctly reads 'f(r)=(S+P/r)/(S+P)'.
evidence: Caption text on PDF 262: "the in-plot note's f(r)=S+P/r)/(S+P) uses P = 40%" (paren count: 2 opens, 3 closes). In-plot green note in panel (a): 'f(r)=(S+P/r)/(S+P)' (3 opens, 3 closes).
acceptance_test: Caption prints f(r)=(S+P/r)/(S+P), paren-balanced and character-identical to the in-plot note.

figure: Figure 17.1 (Sizing a fleet of one model)
issue: The red 'burst peak ~5.5 req/s' label sits in the path of the offered-load curve: the curve passes through the label's vertical band at both ends of the text (t ≈ 5 and t ≈ 7), leaving only a few pixels of clearance at 150 dpi; a glyph/curve intersection cannot be ruled out at this resolution.
evidence: Rendered page (PDF 302) plus curve estimate: burst profile peaks at 5.5 at t = 6 and is ≈0 at t = 2 and t = 10, implying σ ≈ 1.5 h; curve value at t = 5 and t = 7 ≈ 4.3 req/s, inside the label's estimated band (≈4.2–4.8 req/s), and the label spans approximately t ≈ 4.9–7.1 at in-plot type size.
acceptance_test: At 300 dpi, no intersection between the offered-load curve path and the glyph bounding boxes of 'burst peak ~5.5 req/s'; if touching, lower the label by ~0.5 req/s, shorten/reposition it, or add a white halo behind the text.

evidence: Rendered page (PDF 262): the annotation block occupies the upper-left of panel (b) and its last lines sit in the same vertical band as the curve at x ≈ 7–10 (curve ≈ 45–55 a.u. there); the block's longest lines extend to x ≈ 8 on the log axis.
